title: Fast-Path Escalation and Restoration Index
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page defines the "Fast-Path" incident lanes, escalation rules, runbook index, and pre-baked communication templates used by Redwood Inference responders to shorten time-to-containment and accelerate restoration for high-impact customer-facing degradations. It is intended for first responders, on-call SREs, and incident commanders.

Scope:
- Applies to service-impacting incidents that cause user-visible errors or major latency regressions for the Redwood API, Dedicated ingestion, or Console.
- Not intended for scheduled maintenance, developer-only defects, or low-priority internal alerts.

Goals:
- Contain customer impact within the first 15 minutes for Fast-Path incidents.
- Stable mitigation within 60 minutes.
- Complete restoration or defined workaround within the agreed SLA window.

Key concepts and lanes:
1) Fast-Path lane (high priority)
   - Trigger: page is fired for SEV-1 or aggregated SEV-2 (see severity table).
   - Objective: immediate triage, short-lived mitigation (eg. circuit-break, scale-up), notify customers within 20 minutes.

2) Stabilize-Path lane (medium priority)
   - Trigger: service degradation that does not cause customer-visible errors for >50% of requests but threatens SLOs.
   - Objective: apply configuration mitigations, enable fallbacks, and run short experiments to reduce error rate.

3) Restore-Path lane (investigative)
   - Trigger: incidents requiring code rollback, model rollback, or deeper hardware/network interventions.
   - Objective: coordinate multi-team rollouts and perform postmortem action tracking.

Severity classification (quick reference):
- SEV-1: System-wide outage or API failure affecting >30% of requests or major customer SLA breaches. Immediate page to oncall.
- SEV-2: Partial outage or significant latency increase for important routes, causing user-visible degradation for >10% of requests.
- SEV-3: Non-critical feature failures, isolated customer impacts, or degraded background jobs.
- SEV-4: Informational, logging, or development issues.

Escalation matrix (timing expectations):
1) Initial page -> Primary responder acknowledges within 3 minutes.
2) If not acknowledged within 5 minutes -> page escalates to secondary (team lead).
3) On SEV-1: Incident Commander (IC) declared within 6 minutes. IC assembles bridge and contact list.
4) If mitigation not progressing within 15 minutes -> invoke Rapid Exec Notification (product + ops execs).

Roles and responsibilities:
- Primary Responder: first on the page, owns earliest triage steps and updates the incident board.
- Incident Commander (IC): owns outcome, run-of-play, customer comm cadence, and postmortem assignment.
- SRE Liaison: implements autoscaling, cache flushes, traffic re-routing, and infra-level mitigations.
- Comms Owner: prepares status page updates and customer emails; coordinates with CSM if enterprise customers impacted.
- Engineering SMEs: subject matter experts for affected service, model, or infra.

Runbook index (fast access):
- inference-gateway: "inference-gateway-fast-lane" runbook — check upstream model routing, verify token queue lengths, restart gateway pods selectively.
- model-router: "model-router-rollback" — validate model variants, inspect KV cache health, revert to stable variant.
- kv-cache: "kv-cache-eviction-and-rebuild" — review eviction logs, resume population jobs, scale mem-tier.
- auth-service: "auth-service-session-restore" — inspect token store, key rotation checks, identity provider fallbacks.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm scope: routes and customers affected (use: /observability/alerts and the traces/metrics dashboard).
2) Set incident severity and lane.
3) Run top-5 checks: service health, error rates, p95/p99 latency, recent deploys, infra capacity.
4) Apply zero-risk mitigations (circuit breakers, traffic split, restart a small subset).
5) Post initial status update to internal bridge + status page stub.

Command snippets and examples:
- Start an incident in the tracking system: rwd-ops incident create --service inference-gateway --sev 1 --summary "API 503s for customer A"
- Snapshot logs: rwd-ops capture logs --service inference-gateway --since 15m --out /tmp/incident-logs.tar.gz
- Trigger limited rollback (example): kubectl -n prod set image deploy/inference-gw inference-gw=redwood/inference-gw:stable-20260112

Operational SLO thresholds (response policy):
- P99 latency (API generation): 750 ms — if p99 > 1.5x target for >10 minutes escalate to SEV-2.
- Error rate: >1% 5xx on core API endpoints for 5 continuous minutes escalates to SEV-1.
- Background ingestion lag: >30 minutes median for >60 minutes -> SEV-3.

Handoff checklist (on rotation change):
- Handoff owner fills: current incidents (IDs), status, next steps, pending actions, and oncall coverage windows.
- Share ephemeral tokens and credentials only via approved vault tools.
- Ensure runbook links and playbook snippets are pinned in the bridge.

Game day templates and cadence:
- Quarterly full-stack game day (2 hours): simulate model-router regression, validate rollback flows, and test customer comms.
- Monthly micro-drill (30 minutes): practice Fast-Path lane triage and status page update.
- Game day agenda: 1) inject incident, 2) observe alerts, 3) complete Fast-Path checklist, 4) verify status page and customer email path, 5) retro (15 min).

Postmortem and learning loop (required for SEV-1/SEV-2):
- Timeline: publish draft within 72 hours; final postmortem with action owners and dates within two weeks.
- Required sections: Summary, Impact, Root Cause, Timeline of events, Mitigations taken, Action items (owner + due date), Follow-ups (testing & runbook updates).
- Severity review: include SLO impact calculation and whether alert thresholds should change.

Status page templates (short & long forms):
- Short status (for initial page - use on status.redwooodinference.com):
  - Title: "Investigating: API errors in generation endpoints"
  - Impact: "Some customers experiencing 502/503 errors for text generation. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff."
  - Latest: "We are investigating the issue and will provide an update within 20 minutes."

- Long status (follow-up - include technical notes):
  - Title: "Partial outage affecting model routing for generation"
  - Impact: "~18% of requests returned 5xx from inference-gateway; enterprise customers X, Y affected. No data loss."
  - Current status: "Traffic has been diverted to stable model variants; error rate reduced by 70%. Full restoration work continues."
  - Next update: "In 30 minutes or sooner."

Customer email template (enterprise incident notification):
- Subject: "Redwood Inference incident: Partial service degradation impacting text generation (ID: {{incident_id}})"
- Body: "Hello {{customer_name}},

We’re investigating an ongoing partial degradation impacting text generation for some requests. Impact: intermittent 5xx errors and higher latencies. Our teams have applied a traffic diversion to stable variants which reduced errors by ~70% and we are tracking restoration as the primary objective.

What we are doing:
- Active mitigation: traffic diversion and selective rollbacks.
- Next update by: {{next_update_time}}

We apologize for the disruption. If you have questions or need priority assistance, reply to this email and we will route to your CSM/Support lead.

— Redwood Inference Ops"

Post-incident runbook maintenance:
- Every action item that changes a runbook must include: rationale, test steps, rollback, and runbook owner.
- Runbook review cadence: Fast-Path runbooks reviewed at least once per quarter; all others: bi-annual. Add tags for last-reviewed date.

Metrics and dashboards responders should check first:
- api.gateway.errors.5xx (1m, 5m)
- api.gateway.latency.p99
- model.router.queuesize and kv.cache.hit_rate
- infra.gpu.utilization and node.autoscale_events

Communications best practices:
- Use plain language on public status updates; do not include internal trace IDs.
- For enterprise customers, include a short technical appendix in the first follow-up update.
- Keep updates cadence consistent (every 20–30 minutes until stable).

Governance and ownership:
- ICs rotate between eng-sre and eng-platform on a monthly schedule.
- All SEV-1 incidents automatically create an action item in the incident backlog owned by the IC for initial triage.

Appendix: sample incident timeline (example)
- 00:00 Alert fired for inference-gateway 5xx spike.
- 00:01 Primary responder acknowledges; initial triage identifies model-router as a likely suspect.
- 00:04 IC declared; bridge created; customers notified with short status.
- 00:10 Traffic split applied to stable model variant (divert 20%). Errors drop 40%.
- 00:35 Rolling revert of last deploy for model-router; errors down to baseline.
- 01:10 Incident declared resolved; retrospective scheduled and draft postmortem created.

Related resources and links:
- Runbook index (internal): /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/index
- Incident tracker and templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026

If you find ambiguities or gaps in this index, propose edits and tag the oncall-and-incident-response team for review.
